situation.person: Woman in the first two weeks after a C-section, home without nearby family support ('no village'), often with a partner back at work within days
situation.specific_situation: Recovering from major abdominal surgery while solely carrying newborn care - lifting rules, pain schedule, incision checks, feeding round the clock - alone
situation.trigger: Discharge from hospital into an empty house
situation.problem: She does not know what is safe to do, how to manage pain and movement solo, what normal healing looks like versus infection, and collapses under the load by day 4
situation.failed_attempt: Tried to run the pre-baby household at pre-baby speed; paid for it with agony and tears - or lay frozen in bed afraid to move at all
situation.emotional_stake: Terrified of reopening the wound, being rushed back to superwoman duties, or that needing help proves she has failed as a mother
situation.desired_transformation: A day-by-day survival-and-function plan she can execute ALONE: pain on schedule, safe movement, clean incision watch, minimum-viable household - and clear red flags that end guesswork

current_behavior: Lying frozen in bed fearing movement

new_capabilities: Runs a scheduled pain-movement-rest system solo
Performs daily red-flag scan in under a minute
remaining_limits: Some days will simply be hard
evidence_of_change: Meds taken on schedule >=90% of days

mechanism.core_mechanism: Convert surgical recovery into a checklist-driven operating system: scheduled analgesia prevents pain spirals; graduated movement prevents clots; observable red-flag criteria replace fear; Minimum Mode absorbs bad days without collapse
mechanism.why_it_should_work: Standard surgical-recovery principles (scheduled analgesia, early ambulation, wound surveillance) are exactly what a solo patient needs as defaults rather than judgment calls

evidence_basis.claim: Scheduled paracetamol+ibuprofen standard post-C-section and generally compatible with breastfeeding
Early walking recommended to reduce clot risk; avoid lifting >10-15 lb / heavier than baby ~2 weeks; no baths until healed
evidence_basis.source: Cleveland Clinic C-section recovery timeline (2021); Mayo Clinic

evidence_basis.claim: Infection signs: fever >=38C, spreading incision redness/swelling/discharge, worsening pain; calf/chest signs suggest clot - urgent care
evidence_basis.source: WebMD post-C-section recovery warning signs; Medical News Today wound infection review

evidence_basis.claim: Baby blues typically ease within two weeks; beyond that or severe symptoms warrants clinical contact

transformation_path.objective: Build Landing Zone + med schedule before exhaustion hits
Shower, short outdoor walks, visitor protocol live
Light routine, week-2 check-up booked, driving question answered
Any collapse triggers Minimum Mode, not guilt

failure_point_map.scenario: Felt great day 5, cleaned house, wrecked by evening
failure_point_map.rescue_protocol: Minimum Mode next 48h; meds on clock; note the lesson; resume ladder one step lower

failure_point_map.scenario: Breastfeeding fear or forgetfulness stopped analgesia
failure_point_map.rescue_protocol: Re-read sourced compatibility note; set phone alarms; call clinician line if still uneasy
Decision Card section 1 routing - clinician today / emergency now
Script 7 said aloud to one human; rescue-card numbers if darkening

failure_point_map.failure_type: helper applies cultural remedy to wound
failure_point_map.rescue_protocol: Rinse clean water if fresh, photograph, Decision Card, reset script, log

first_win.action: Build the Landing Zone: chair/bed corner stocked with 48 hours of water, snacks, nappies, wipes, charger - plus tonight's med alarm set
first_win.observable_change: Next baby-care cycle happens entirely inside the zone without a single cross-house trip

before_baseline: can name incision red flags yes/no
success_indicators: all red flags got same-day response
tsm.success_threshold: 60%+ completers meet >=3 of 4 indicators at Day 14/30 review
tsm.measurement_method: Daily one-line log + structured Day-14 check against baseline
tsm.incomplete_progress_interpretation: Bad days are data not failure; only ignored red flags or repeated over-lifts reset progress to Survive phase
tsm.next_action_on_miss: Drop one rung on the movement ladder for 48h and re-run Setup

maintenance.maintenance_system: Weeks 3-6: weekly self-review against lifting/driving/exercise clearance questions until 6-week sign-off
maintenance.relapse_protocol: Post-week-14 overexertion flare: 48h Minimum Mode, escalate only per Decision Card
maintenance.reentry_protocol: Restart at Function phase with whoever now helps; no guilt

evidence.source: Mayo Clinic; Cleveland Clinic 2021; WebMD recovery guidance

safety.scope_boundary: Coordinates solo recovery logistics ONLY. Never diagnoses infection/clots/depression, never adjusts prescriptions, never replaces the week-2 visit or 6-week clearance.
red_flags: soaking-a-pad-per-hour bleeding, large clots, foul lochia
blues past two weeks or thoughts of harm
escalation_rules: Fever + any incision sign = same hour
Mood crisis lines from verified shared list always active

research_disposition.rationale: Flagship #5 (score 80). Hidden market verbatim: 'How do I function normally again after a C-section while caring for a newborn?' Renamed per naming audit.

evidence_refs: Mayo Clinic; Cleveland Clinic 2021; WebMD recovery guidance
